simple.meaning: רוּחַ (rûwach) appears 11 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a son in the family line and in connection with kingship. The occurrence trail connects the name with an offering.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Deuteronomy, Judges, and 5 more, beginning at Genesis 8:21. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family line, offering, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רוּחַ (H7306) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows רוּחַ through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: רוּחַ (rûwach) / H7306 is tracked through Genesis 8:21, Genesis 27:27, Exodus 30:38, Leviticus 26:31. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

He came near, and kissed him. He smelled the smell of his clothing, and blessed him, and said,
Whoever shall make any like that, to smell of it, he shall be cut off from his people.”
I will lay your cities waste, and will bring your sanctuaries to desolation. I will not take delight in the sweet fragrance of your offerings.
There you shall serve gods, the work of men’s hands, wood and stone, which neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.
